newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch swine fever set to raise Europe pork prices.
newsitem.headline: Dutch swine fever set to raise Europe pork prices.

text.p: Pork supplies in the Netherlands are becoming seriously tight as a result of a swine fever epidemic that has decimated the pig population and threatens to push up meat prices across Europe.
Dutch slaughterhouses are paying four guilders a kilo for pigs, up from 2.80 guilders at the beginning of the year. On the British market, prices have risen by more than 10 percent since early March.

"Dutch prices have gone up sharply, particularly in the last week and it is having an effect elsewhere in Europe -- from Germany through to France and Italy," said Arian Wissman, analyst at the Dutch government's Agricultural Economics Institute.
In Dutch retail outlets, pork prices have been held down so far, but retailers say this cannot last for long.

"If the current situation continues, then it would be strange if the price for the consumer would not go up as well. We expect this to happen very soon," said a spokeswoman for Albert Heijn, the country's largest retail chain.

The market impact has been exacerbated by an outbreak of the same disease in Germany and a switch in some EU exports to Japan, whose traditional supplier Taiwan has been hit by a foot-and-mouth epidemic and had to halt its own exports.
"A lot of Danish pork is now going to Japan instead of into Europe," Wissman added. "They get a good price for their meat."

The effects have also been felt in the U.S., where lean hogs and pork bellies are traded on the Chicago exchange. News of supply tightness in Europe and a shortage in Japan has pushed prices up around 20 percent to new contract highs.

The Netherlands is one of Europe's leading exporters of pigs and pork, earning some 5.1 billion guilders from the trade last year. Before the swine fever outbreak -- detected in February -- there were some 14 million pigs in the country.
Since February many of the Netherlands' trading partners including the U.S. have banned imports of Dutch pigs and pork.
The Netherlands has destroyed at least one million pigs in an effort to curb the swine fever outbreak, which has now spread to 121 farms.
The government has called in the army to help transport animals to slaughterhouses and banned livestock movements in most of the southern Netherlands.
Strict controls are in place around infected areas, which cover more than 1,600 farms. It is the country's first outbreak of the highly contagious disease since 1992.
